name: dialogue
description: YarnSpinner dialogue with content pipeline importer, runner, and HUD UI
postInstallNotes:
## dialogue installed

**Content pipeline.** Your project DLL must be referenced by MGCB so it can load the YarnSpinner importer/processor. Add to your csproj:
```xml
<PropertyGroup>
  <MonoGameMGCBAdditionalArguments>$(MonoGameMGCBAdditionalArguments) /reference:$(MSBuildThisFileDirectory)bin/$(Configuration)/net8.0/$(AssemblyName).dll</MonoGameMGCBAdditionalArguments>
</PropertyGroup>
```
The `CopyLocalLockFileAssemblies`, `EnableDynamicLoading`, and `GenerateRuntimeConfigurationFiles` properties are required for the importer to load YarnSpinner's transitive dependencies — this module adds them automatically.

**Yarn assets.** Author `.yarn` files in `Content/Dialogues/`, then in your `.mgcb`:
```
#begin Dialogues/intro.yarn
/importer:YarnSpinnerImporter
/processor:YarnSpinnerProcessor
/build:Dialogues/intro.yarn
```

**Runtime wiring.** Load yarn programs via `content.Load<YarnProgram>(...)`, then construct `DialogueSystem` with the runner, font, dialog-box texture, indicator texture, and input bindings (see the constructor signature). Add it to your update pipeline AFTER input, BEFORE rendering.

**Triggering dialogue.** This module is game-agnostic — it does not own the *when* a dialogue starts. Implement a small game-side system that publishes `DialogueStartMessage` in response to your trigger (collision zone, NPC interaction, scripted event). See `MonoDreams.Examples/System/Dialogue/ZoneDialogueTriggerSystem.cs` for the canonical collision-zone pattern.
